fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Like the priest-craft of old, modern medicine is based on arcane systems of thought, invisible causes, and fabricated histories. Genetics, epidemics, germs, and all those diseases we allegedly cured are founded on some very flexible statistics...
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Dr. Marizelle Arce returns to InnerVerse for another great chat about the history of medicine's divergent terrain vs. germ philosophies. We discuss environmental and lifestyle factors of health, misconceptions about genetics and "viruses", the worldview influence of false historical narratives, pleomorphism and microbial adaptability, and much more. In Part 2 we discuss German New Medicine, parenting and childhood health from the terrain and holistic perspective, mind-body relationship significance, what earwax tells the terrain doctor, and whether or not EMF is dangerous.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "What German New Medicine Gets Right and Where It Hardens", "body": "Chance opens hour two by asking for honest feedback on German new medicine, and Arce answers that she dabbled in it, owns books on it, and finds it hits home wherever it stays with patterns rather than turning into an end-all be-all. Her objection is rigidity, because if perception differs from person to person then two people should not be expected to produce the same physiological response to the same conflict. Chance compares it to biofield anatomy, where every human being is a different painting made from the same seven colors, and both agree that dogma, branding and ownership are ego rather than knowledge."}, {"title": "Separation, Not Germs, in the Nursery", "body": "Arce brings up a Huffington Post headline about toddlers catching up to nineteen illnesses in their first year at nursery and argues there is nothing to catch, only a small body responding to a foreign environment without its mother. She notes that children do not regulate their own temperature until roughly age three, which is why families in indigenous cultures slept together for warmth and security. Chance points out that the mainstream reads the same statistic as an immune system developing, and both say the common factor left out of the article is the separation itself."}, {"title": "Shame, Forgiveness and Advice From a Vanished World", "body": "Much of the second hour turns to the guilt aimed at mothers and the resistance older parents show when their grown children bring them new information. Arce's answer is forgiveness, since you did the best you could with what you knew, you forgive yourself, and you mirror that forgiveness to your child. Chance describes the wall he hits with his parents' generation, where entertaining a new idea feels like admitting that a life was a lie. Arce adds that advice built for a different economy, school system and era is a used candle, offered lovingly but no longer usable."}, {"title": "Earwax and the Language of Symptoms", "body": "Arce treats earwax the way she treats every other fluid of the body, as a measure of flow. Dried wax reads to her as stagnation, excess or blockage as a body working something out, and a little runniness during a cold as the process doing its job. Her broader claim is that symptoms are signs rather than enemies, a language telling you what is going on instead of a problem to silence. Chance connects it to his daughter's gentle chiropractic care, and Arce says the parent who watches closely is the ultimate naturopath in the home."}, {"title": "The EMF Boogeyman and the Biofield", "body": "Asked to name the biggest boogeyman in alternative health, Chance lands on EMF, and Arce says she has never been affected by it and is instead the one affecting it, freezing her husband's computers whenever she got upset. Clients who arrived sensitive grew less sensitive, she says, as their nervous systems settled and their own field became more coherent. Chance argues that EMF functionally reduces to light, sound and heat, and that the 5G panic was handed to alternative media the way other narratives are. Both land on responsibility for the internal environment over blaming the external thing."}]
